REVIEW RESULT
MAIN, RESEARCH-INDEX, RESULT-LEDGER, active T11 ROUTE and complete research-card161 agree on the frontier. Card160 controls only a high-squarefree-kernel energy sector and does not bound principal class1. Card161 controls only endpoints with a short primitive face hypotenuse; the complementary endpoints remain unbounded at the required scale. Neither is a whole-population closure.


Whole-population candidates exist, but no new executable saving mechanism was obtained in this review. M3-A-001 is a PAUSED sufficient receiver on the exact directional two-face host, requiring correlation decay with a one-twelfth margin. M3-A-GATE-001 explicitly requires a same-physical-measure correlation theorem or a valid coefficient adapter. M3-A-LOCAL-001 only controls known local blocker interaction, not correlation of the actual global completion predicates. Thus A001 is not an available proved aggregate estimate, and is NOT declared impossible or exhausted.


For clarity, the original unsplit directional selector table can be kept intact. Write a=M3(B), b=M2,j(B), n=N2,j(B), p=P(B), N=a+b. Its four cell counts are p,a-p,n,b-n. If F is the third-face indicator and S the space-diagonal indicator, then
Cov(F,S)=(b*p-a*n)/N^2,
and, when both variances are nonzero,
rho=(b*p-a*n)/sqrt(a*b*(p+n)*(N-p-n)).
These follow directly from E(F)=a/N, E(S)=(p+n)/N, E(FS)=p/N. They are an algebraic diagnostic of the retained receiver, NOT a new theorem or research credit: the unknown endpoint count p is still inside the numerator. Centering or applying Cauchy-Schwarz alone only yields |rho|<=1, not the decay demanded by A001. No new physical cancellation or same-measure transfer was proved.


Other retained aggregate targets remain conditional:157 needs actual same-M3 two-prime correlation control;158 records obstacles for the attempted transfer;159 does not globally exclude pre-endpoint multivariable methods; TQ-GATE-002 needs genuine global squareclass incidence, and TQ005/tH14 do not supply it merely by restricting to principal1. This review makes no literature-wide no-go claim.

A new label for an unproved correlation/energy bound is insufficient. Do not automatically reactivate on a generic continuation command without first honoring this whole-population requirement.

M3-T11-161 — SUMMED PRINCIPAL SHORT-PRIMITIVE-FACE THEOREM
MEASURE=ORIGINAL physical H_F(B) before H-square, all content/physical/chart masks preserved. On class1 let g=gcd(C,X),c0=C/g,x0=X/g,p0=sqrt(c0^2+x0^2). Integer principal norm implies p0 integral and p0<=R<=B. This is a single state's primitive missing-face hypotenuse.
PROOF161.1=Every primitive ordered positive Pythagorean vector with p0<=T is, up to two leg orders, (m^2-n^2,2mn,m^2+n^2),m>n>0,coprime,opposite parity. Both parameters<=sqrt(T),so at most2T ordered directions. Each direction has one reduced positive ratio rho. ROUTE14.1/010 uniformly bounds its full physical fiber m_rho(B)<=K_epsilon B^epsilon,including all lifts/contents. Thus r_1,<=T<=2K_epsilon T B^epsilon for everyepsilon>0. No hidden family sum.
PROOF161.2=For each canonical endpoint define p_ij=sqrt(e_i^2+e_j^2)/gcd(e_i,e_j). Choose a minimum p_ij with deterministic canonical tie break. Complementary edge Y and other two integral faces plus integral space diagonal give the retained160 first-cover state, with kappa1. Parent retention gives injective parent charging into short states (harmless fixed chart constant). Therefore P_short(p_min<=T)<=O(r_1,<=T)<=T B^o. This is a sufficiency theorem and scope audit, not a proved character-sum estimate or a claim of a new sieve method.


## 1. Exact zero-free terminal character
For each primitive Euler brick E, let X be its unique odd edge and Y,Z its even edges, D^2=Y^2+Z^2 and
 T(E)=X^2+Y^2+Z^2=X^2+D^2.
T is an integer even when the physical diagonal sqrt(T) is not integral. For every inert prime p=3 mod4,
 p does NOT divide T(E).                                      (157.1)
Proof: if p|X^2+D^2, anisotropy of a sum of two squares modulo p forces p|X,D. From D^2=Y^2+Z^2 it then forces p|Y,Z, contradicting primitivity. The argument is uniform for all primitive M3, not just endpoints.
Thus chi_p(T(E)) is always +1 or -1; there is no zero-terminal stratum. Divisibility of individual edges by p is still allowed and cannot be discarded as negligible. The inert norm argument is reused elementary structure, not credited as novel.


Every endpoint has T=R^2 and hence chi_p(T)=+1 for every inert p. This is a necessary condition only.


## 2. Whole-M3 second-moment certificate
For a FIXED finite set S of k distinct inert primes, write
 C_pq(B)=M3(B)^(-1) sum_{E in M3(B)} chi_p(T(E))*chi_q(T(E)), p!=q.
Set F_S(E)=sum_{p in S} chi_p(T(E)). Every endpoint contributes k^2 to F_S(E)^2; all other contributions are nonnegative. Therefore
 P(B)/M3(B) <= 1/k + (2/k^2) sum_{p<q in S} C_pq(B).    (157.2)
Proof: k^2 P<=sum_E F_S(E)^2. Expanding the square and using(157.1), each diagonal term is exactly M3(B). No asymptotic, residue uniformity, or independence was used.


For any real weights w_p with W=sum w_p!=0 there is also the exact finite-B bound
 P/M3 <= [sum w_p^2+2sum_{p<q} w_p w_q C_pq]/W^2.       (157.3)
It follows by applying the same argument to sum w_p chi_p(T). Only fixed weights are used in the ordered-limit applications here; no uncontrolled adaptive optimization is promoted.


A sufficient global theorem is: for fixed sets S_k with |S_k|=k,
 lim_{k→infinity} limsup_{B→infinity}
 [1/k+(2/k^2)sum_{p<q in S_k} C_pq(B)] =0.             (157.4)
Then P/M3→0. All primes in S_k are fixed before taking B→infinity. No theorem uniform in a B-dependent modulus is required. A sufficient stronger version is pairwise C_pq(B)→0 for every distinct pair in an infinite inert-prime sequence. More generally only the averaged positive correlations need decay; exact zero for every fixed pair is unnecessary.


One-prime marginals alone cannot establish(157.4): an abstract population with probability1/2 at the all-plus sign vector and1/2 at all-minus has zero marginal means, pair correlations1, and all-plus mass1/2 at every k. This is a logical countermodel to inferring joint contraction from marginals, not a construction of actual Euler bricks.


The original rho^k full-block contraction remains a sufficient theorem. It is stronger than what is needed for this particular closure mechanism. We do NOT claim(157.4) implies exponential block contraction, or that the certificates are mathematically equivalent.


## 3. Automatic primes and the local measure
At p=3, the nonzero squares are {1}; two nonzero edges would have a face norm2, a nonsquare. Thus at most one edge is nonzero modulo3, and chi_3(T)=1 on every primitive M3 object.
At p=11, nonzero square values are {1,3,4,5,9}. Two such values can have square sum exactly along the five-cycle
 1—3—9—5—4—1.
There are no loops because2 is a nonsquare, and no triangles. Hence three nonzero edge squares cannot have all pair sums square: every Euler brick has an edge divisible by11. With that edge zero modulo11, T is an existing face square and is nonzero by(157.1). Consequently
 chi_11(T)=1 on ALL primitive M3.                       (157.5)
These primes supply no terminal selection. Small-prime divisibility facts are treated as elementary reused/scoped checks, not a literature-wide discovery. A theorem claiming zero character means at EVERY inert prime is false; sufficiently good selected primes may omit3 and11. No claim is made that these are the only automatic primes.


The exact half-set size |Omega_p|=(p+1)/2 is on uniform P1(Fp). It is NOT the same as conditional uniform Euler/K3 reduction. We checked the latter explicitly as a CANDIDATE local model:
 normalize the first nonzero edge coordinate to1;
 sum over edge residues (a,b,c);
 w_p(a,b,c)=product_{pairs}(1+chi_p(a_i^2+a_j^2)).
This is the exact number of face-root lifts in the projective six-coordinate Euler model. Put Z_p=sum w_p and A_p=sum w_p chi_p(a^2+b^2+c^2), delta_p=A_p/Z_p.


| p | Z_p | A_p | delta_p |
|---|---:|---:|---|
|3|12|12|1|
|7|92|28|7/23|
|11|108|108|1|
|19|396|12|1/33|
|23|668|92|23/167|


For example, in this finite model the terminal pass fraction at7 is15/23, not1/2; at11 it is1. The projective selector half-set formula is retained; only a mistaken identification of measures is excluded.
These finite field values are exact exhaustive certificates at the displayed primes. They are NOT measurements or asymptotics of M3(B), do not prove equidistribution, and are not used to extrapolate delta_p→0.
Uniform finite CRT product models have pair means delta_p delta_q, not necessarily0. Thus even if an eventual physical transfer matches this model, demanding EXACT zero for each fixed pair can be too strong. A valid bias-aware statement C_pq=delta_p delta_q+o(1), coupled with proved Cesaro-small biases, would suffice for(157.4). Neither physical transfer nor the infinite-prime bias theorem is established here.


## 4. A concrete integer kernel preserving the physical masks
Reuse M3-DIV-001. For positive odd X, choose divisors a,b of X^2 with0<a,b<X and define
 Y=(X^2/a-a)/2, Z=(X^2/b-b)/2.
Retain Y<Z, gcd(X,Y,Z)=1, Y^2+Z^2=square, and T<=B^2. The two X-face squares are automatic, while the remaining third-face square is an essential mask. The unique odd edge and ordering of even edges give multiplicity one for the canonical M3 object, independent of where X falls in sorted physical order.
Let
 K(X,a,b)=4X^2+(X^2/a-a)^2+(X^2/b-b)^2=4T.             (157.6)
The quotients X^2/a and X^2/b are evaluated as INTEGERS before reduction; do not invert a or b modulo a prime, since they may be divisible by it.


For m=pq, p!=q inert, the exact required numerator in(157.2) is
 W_m(B)=sum_{odd X,a,b|X^2, ALL physical masks above} chi_m(K(X,a,b)),
 C_pq(B)=W_pq(B)/M3(B).                                (157.7)
Here chi_m is the Jacobi product chi_p chi_q and chi_m(4)=1. This adapter has no fixed-power loss and preserves the denominator, cutoff, primitive/canonical weighting and square locus. The divisor encoding itself is reused, not new counting credit.


The obstacle is now explicit: obtain cancellation for(157.7) on the physical THIRD-FACE-SQUARE locus. Ambient complete sums or ordinary divisor correlations before that mask do not evaluate this numerator. Boundary estimates for a continuous parameter region alone do not resolve the square mask. The old corrected-frozen Davenport argument cannot be cited.

# M3-T11-156 — R502 carrier obstruction to the uniform raw cross-gcd tail

## Authority and decision
Fresh MAIN/INDEX/RESULT-LEDGER/active T11 ROUTE designate155. The subsequent full CARD-INDEX portfolio audit recommends an exact cross-gcd tail preflight. This card performs that test against the actual Stage14 square-root proof and the retained R502 family. It derives a new quantitative LOWER bound for a raw tail, not a new endpoint upper bound.


There are constants kappa,k>0 such that, for every sufficiently large B,
 E_raw,{c>kappa sqrt(B)}(B) >= k B^(1/4).                 (156.1)
Consequently the proposed bound E_raw,{c>C}(B)<=B^(1/2+o(1)) C^(-1+o(1)), UNIFORMLY over all C, is FALSE. More generally it fails at C=B^gamma for every fixed 1/4<gamma<1/2.
The minimal useful single-threshold target C=B^(1/6+eta), with 0<eta<1/12, is NOT refuted. That narrower target is still open and does not follow from the unstratified proof. Do not mark all XG-GATE-002 formulations false, and do not infer failure of an endpoint-only tail from a raw-tail counterexample.


## 1. Scope match of the existing half-power theorem
AR-006 explicitly states an exactly-two N2 theorem and cannot alone be quoted as a raw graph bound. Reading Stage14 Final R06, Lemmas3.1/3.2, Proposition3.6 and its final proof fills this scope adapter: E=N2+3T, E<=V B^o(1), V<=B^(1/2+o(1)). Thus E<=B^(1/2+o(1)) on the full raw graph, and P<=E/3 remains valid. No retraction of the existing endpoint ceiling is justified.
Stage14-X13 charges common core, primitive agreement pair and one reconstructed column; reverse reciprocal completion has B^o(1) multiplicity. These complete counts do not contain a new bound for the distribution of c_raw. The old historical cross-root H is not identified with c_raw.


## 2. Reuse the existing R502 family
For coprime positive m,n with 7/2<m/n<4, put
 A=(m^4-n^4)(m^4-81n^4),
 B0=4mn(m^2-3n^2)(m^4+2m^2n^2+9n^4),
 C0=16m^2n^2(m^4-9n^4),
 D1=m^8+46m^4n^4+81n^8,
 D2=4mn(m^2-3n^2)(m^4+10m^2n^2+9n^4),
 D=(m^4-2m^2n^2+9n^4)(m^4+10m^2n^2+9n^4).
Exact identities:
 A^2+C0^2=D1^2, B0^2+C0^2=D2^2, A^2+B0^2+C0^2=D^2. (156.2)
The fixed cone has 0<A<B0<C0; this is the source R502 cone. Divide by g=gcd(A,B0,C0). The primitive cuboid has R=D/g and two integer faces, with no condition on its third face needed here. Divisibility of every diagonal by g follows primewise from g^2 dividing its square.


Let g1=gcd(A,C0), g2=gcd(B0,C0), K=4mn(m^2-3n^2),
 J=(m^2+n^2)(m^2+9n^2), L=(m^2-n^2)(m^2-9n^2).
Then A=JL, D2=KJ. Also
 g2=K e, e=gcd(m^4+2m^2n^2+9n^4,4mn(m^2+3n^2)).
Write b=1 if m,n both odd, else0; a=1 if3|m, else0. Exact formulas are
 g1=2^(7b)3^(4a)<=10368, e=2^(2b)3^(2a)<=36.           (156.3)
These formulas are proved below, not inferred from a finite census.


The two reduced primitive faces sharing the physical C0 edge are
 F1=(C0/g1,A/g1,D1/g1), F2=(C0/g2,B0/g2,D2/g2).
Their cross-gcd factors are c12=gcd(D1/g1,B0/g2) and c21=gcd(D2/g2,A/g1).
Since D2/g2=J/e and A/g1=JL/g1, put u=J/e,v=JL/g1. The identity g1 v=e u L implies u|g1 v, so u/gcd(u,v) divides g1. Therefore
 c_raw=c12 c21>=c21>=J/(e g1)>=J/373248.                (156.4)
This arithmetic inequality survives primitive reduction and measures the actual raw edge, not an ambient parameter lattice.


### Proof of (156.3)
For any p>3, p|m or p|n makes A and the quartic norm factor units modulo p, so cannot contribute. If p does not divide mn and p|C0, then m^4=9n^4 modulo p. The two factors of A become8n^4 and -72n^4; neither vanishes for p>3. Hence g1 has no prime>3.
For e, again a prime dividing mn cannot divide its quartic F=m^4+2m^2n^2+9n^4 unless p=3. If p>3 divides m^2+3n^2, substitution gives F=12n^4 modulo p. Thus e also has no prime>3.
At2, opposite parity makes A and F odd. When both are odd, v2(C0)=7 while both factors of A have valuation at least4; hence v2(g1)=7. Also F=12 modulo16, so v2(F)=2, while4mn(m^2+3n^2) has valuation at least4, giving v2(e)=2.
At3, when3 does not divide m, C0 is a3-unit (if3|n also both A and F are units), and either F is a3-unit or the complementary denominator is, so both minima are0.
When3|m with r=v3(m)>=1, v3(C0)=2r+2. The first factor of A is a3-unit; the second has valuation at least4, and exactly4 for r>=2. At r=1 the C0 valuation is4. Hence v3(g1)=4 in every case.
For e, the denominator4mn(m^2+3n^2) has valuation r+1. At r=1, F has valuation at least2 and denominator exactly2; at r>=2, F has valuation exactly2. Hence v3(e)=2. This proves all claims.


## 3. Count actual primitive raw objects
Set T=floor((B/240)^(1/8)). Take n in (T/8,T/4], and m=4n-k with 1<=k<n/2 and gcd(k,n)=1. Then m,n<=T, 7/2<m/n<4, and m>7T/16. The usual Mobius/totient count on this fixed cone gives >>T^2 distinct reduced parameters.
D<=240 T^8, so R=D/g<=B. Also J>=m^4>=(7T/16)^4, and (156.4) implies c_raw>=const*T^4>=const*sqrt(B).
Primitive reduction identifies at most8 of these parameters per canonical cuboid: the largest-edge/space-diagonal ratio is
 C0/D=16t^2(t^4-9)/[(t^4-2t^2+9)(t^4+10t^2+9)], t=m/n,
a nonconstant rational function of degree at most8. For a fixed ratio, its cross-multiplied polynomial has at most8 roots. The cone fixes the largest edge, and this ratio is invariant under primitive scaling. Thus there are >>T^2>>B^(1/4) distinct primitive raw objects and raw edges with large c. Choosing kappa smaller than the resulting constant proves (156.1).
This argument does NOT need Faltings, the third-face-square exception set, a perfect-cuboid example, or a numerical absence result.


## 4. Consequences for globalization budget
At C=kappa sqrt(B), the claimed uniform upper bound is B^o(1), contradicting B^(1/4). At C=B^gamma, 1/4<gamma<1/2, all these objects eventually lie in the tail while the upper bound would be B^(1/2-gamma+o(1))=o(B^(1/4)).
For the intended C=B^(1/6+eta), the proposed upper exponent is1/3-eta. If eta>1/12 (and gamma<1/2), it contradicts this family; if0<eta<1/12, its exponent exceeds1/4, so this family is compatible with that upper bound. At eta=1/12 the exponents agree, so no contradiction is established.
The R502 family itself is only B^(1/4) in power scale, below the M3 lower benchmark B^(1/3). It obstructs the chosen strong RAW certificate, not P/M3→0. Its presence shows why imposing endpoint/M3 masks matters rather than demanding excessive decay of all exactly-two objects.


The other156 budget choices remain blocked with current inputs: absolute-value/divisor bounds on155.5 return the original moving-R circle envelope and do not supply a global cancellation estimate. A denominator improvement merely above1/3 cannot close using the present half-power numerator; a standalone denominator closure needs an exponent strictly above1/2. No new additive or denominator theorem is proved here.

Keep XG-008 identities and the threshold-specific XG problem open for0<eta<1/12, but only reopen it with an actual stratified moment theorem and a small-c/large-tau residual budget.
Next157: test the fixed-finite-inert-prime block relative receiver on exact M3. A sufficient theorem is, for arbitrarily large fixed finite S,
 limsup_{B→∞} M3_accepted(S,B)/M3(B)<=rho^|S|, rho<1,
including bad/zero residues. Fix S before B→∞; then enlarge S. Single-prime marginals alone are not enough. Stage15 M2 congruence asymptotics and ambient parameter CRT do not transfer automatically. The next card must find a genuine physical-measure distribution input or record its missing hypothesis; it must not merely rename this gate.

Starting authority and the test


Fresh MAIN, INDEX, RESULT-LEDGER and active T11 ROUTE all designate154. Its complete card is the current source for the missing same-witness correlation gate.152 and153 remain valid sector theorems. The exact unresolved population is E_bal: primitive canonical positive endpoints at R<=B, some prime outside152's S_B, and R/p^v_p(R)>Y_B for every p|R, with Y_B=B^(1/3)/(1+log B)^30.


155 tests whether enforcing154's shared-edge equality itself supplies a quantitative saving beyond151's original joint Gaussian receiver. It proves an exact gluing formula for arbitrary exponents and cofactors, and an exact equivalence for ALL squarefree split R, with arbitrarily many prime factors. The answer is that compatibility removes independently duplicated witness choices, but the completed local tests reproduce the original sphere equation. No new global or negligible-sector estimate follows. This is not an impossibility theorem for using these representations with a genuinely new analytic estimate.


1. Exact shared-edge gluing, uniformly in the cofactor


Write R=p^n q^m h, p!=q split odd primes, gcd(pq,h)=1, n,m>=1, and all primes of h split. Fix Gaussian primes pi,rho above p,q. Set A=bar(pi)^(2n), D=bar(rho)^(2m), and D(h)=product_(l^a||h)(2a+1). A local p-oriented edge has H_p=A G, Norm(G)=(q^m h)^2; a q-oriented edge has H_q=D L, Norm(L)=(p^n h)^2. The edge is a unit at BOTH p and q.


Same positive edge and complementary-diagonal magnitude means H_p=H_q or H_p=bar(H_q). These pairs have the following complete parametrization:


 H_p=H_q:       G=D K,       L=A K;
 H_p=bar(H_q):  G=bar(D) K,  L=bar(A) bar(K);
 Norm(K)=h^2.                                                (155.1)


Proof: A and D are coprime in Z[i]. In the first equality A G=D L, unique factorization forces D|G and A|L. In the second equality A G=bar(D) bar(L), it forces bar(D)|G and A|bar(L). Substitution gives the displayed K and its norm. Conversely every such K satisfies the required equality and norms. Its p/q valuations are automatically zero because gcd(h,pq)=1.


The two branches are disjoint. Otherwise the common H_q would be real, whereas its q-valuations are0 and2m, impossible for a nonzero real Gaussian integer. Norm(h)>0 excludes zero. The shared H also cannot have zero real part, since a pure imaginary integer has equal valuations at a Gaussian prime and its conjugate.


There are4D(h) Gaussian integers K of norm h^2. Thus the EXACT number of signed oriented pairs is8D(h), and imposing positive common real part leaves4D(h), by the fixed-point-free K->-K involution. This counts oriented representations of one edge, not cuboid endpoints or canonical triples. For h=1 there are8 signed pairs and4 with positive real part, regardless of p,q,n,m.


This replaces the false independent product (8D(h))^2 of two shared-unit cofactor lists by8D(h). It is a genuine removal of duplicate choices. However151 already encodes a triple using a SINGLE global H_i per edge. Those original allocations already contain this compatibility. Since D(h)=h^o(1), the displayed compression supplies no new fixed power of R compared with that original receiver. No such asymptotic estimate is imported as a theorem needed for the gluing proof; the standard divisor-size observation is only explanatory.


2. All squarefree split diagonals: full Gaussian local tests equal the sphere gate


Let R be ANY odd squarefree product of split primes. Select three pairs H_i=e_i+i f_i with positive integer e_i,f_i, Norm(H_i)=R^2, gcd(e_1,e_2,e_3)=1, and exactly ONE odd e_i. These are the original edge/complementary-face circles, before imposing the sphere equation. Any original physical endpoint satisfies these conditions. Define


 F=sum_i(H_i^2+bar(H_i)^2)+2R^2
  =4(sum_i e_i^2-R^2).                                    (155.2)


For p|R choose pi above p. Let I_p={i:p does not divide e_i}. For each i in I_p orient H_i by independently conjugating it so that H_i'=bar(pi)^2 G_i^(p), and put C_p=sum_(i in I_p)(G_i^(p))^2. This orientation exists: if p does not divide e_i, one of the two Gaussian valuations of H_i is0 and the other2. All terms H_i^2+bar(H_i)^2 are unchanged by the conjugations.


The FULL local Gaussian condition obeys


 pi^2 | C_p  iff  pi^2 | F  iff  p^2 | F.                 (155.3)


To see this, modulo pi^2 the conjugates of the oriented unit edges vanish, leaving bar(pi)^4 C_p. For i outside I_p, p divides both e_i and f_i: the norm equation implies p|f_i, so H_i and its conjugate are each divisible by pi and their squares vanish modulo pi^2. Also pi^2|R^2. The factor bar(pi)^4 is invertible modulo pi^2. Finally F is an ordinary integer, so conjugation converts pi^2|F to bar(pi)^2|F, and together these imply p^2|F. This reasoning also handles |I_p|=1; such a tuple cannot pass the local test, because its lone G is a pi-unit.


Taking ALL p|R, squarefreeness and the Chinese remainder theorem yield R^2|F, equivalently R^2|sum e_i^2. Since 0<e_i<R, this sum is strictly between0 and3R^2. Its quotient by R^2 is therefore1 or2. Exactly one odd edge gives sum e_i^2=1 modulo4, while R^2=1 modulo4; quotient2 is impossible. Consequently


 [pi_p^2|C_p for EVERY p|R]  iff  sum_i e_i^2=R^2.       (155.4)


The reverse implication is immediate from F=0 and(155.3). After(155.4), primitivity forces |I_p| in {2,3}, and the positive-edge argument retained in153 gives C_p!=0. Thus requiring these two extra witness filters does not change the equivalence.


Equation(155.4) covers ALL squarefree support sizes at once. It demonstrates why multiplying local probabilities is unjustified here: once the local witnesses reconstruct the same global H_i, demanding all the exact tests is precisely the original physical sphere equation. It does not prove those solutions are frequent, rare, or absent. The weaker integer condition p^2|Norm(C_p) used for candidate upper bounds in153/154 is NOT substituted for the full Gaussian condition.


For nonsquarefree R the same modulo-pi^2 argument still supplies p^2|F, but only rad(R)^2|F after gluing. It does not give R^2|F. Hence(155.4) is not silently extended to repeated-prime-power diagonals. Those remain part of E_bal and still require a bound.


3. What the total budget actually says


Let D(R)=product_(p^a||R)(2a+1). There are4D(R) signed Gaussian circle points per edge. Global triples before the sphere filter therefore cost at most64D(R)^3, exactly the old151/152 allocation envelope. Gluing local orientations into one global triple pays this envelope once; it does not replace it by a proved smaller count of successful sphere triples.


155 provides neither sum_(R<=B,R in E_bal) J(R)=o(M3(B)) nor a negligible new physical sector.154's scalar alphabet-cover obstruction is untouched. Its O(B^(1/2)/log B) balanced semiprime upper budget has not been improved. The prime directions must be consistent, but mere consistency is not a new sparse-population theorem.


Decision: the elementary same-witness/CRT bootstrap FAILS AS A NEW COUNTING MECHANISM. Stop generating successive cards that only add more compatible primes or rewrite the same joint receiver.152/153 remain retained;154's firewalls remain retained; global credit stays0 and the main gate staysOPEN. A future estimate of the already-glued sphere population would reopen this mechanism, but another gluing identity alone does not.


4. Concrete alternative: test additive counting on the exact circle population


For odd split R and d|R define the finite exponential polynomial


 A_(R,d)(theta)=sum_(0<e<R, R^2-e^2=f^2 with f>0, d|e)
                    exp(2*pi*i*e^2*theta).


Orthogonality gives the exact labelled primitive positive cuboid count


 N_prim(R)=sum_(d|R) mu(d) integral_0^1
               exp(-2*pi*i*R^2*theta) A_(R,d)(theta)^3 dtheta. (155.5)


Proof: the integral selects precisely sum e_i^2=R^2 with positive integer complementary diagonals. Each e has one positive f. On such a triple any common divisor g of the edges divides R because g^2 divides R^2; it also divides every f_i. The sum of mu(d) over common divisors d|R of all edges is1 exactly for primitive triples, and0 otherwise. Thus the formula preserves primitivity rather than quietly counting scaled copies. Original canonical masks select a subpopulation, so their physical count is at most N_prim(R). One may retain those masks explicitly for an equality on the original population.


This formula is an EXACT ADAPTER, not a new bound and not a claim of novelty. Dropping phases or taking only absolute-value/divisor bounds returns the old envelope. A useful next study must identify cancellation, additive structure, or a separate stronger denominator estimate that changes the TOTAL exponent on the exact moving-R population. Generic random residues or parameter-side CRT estimates cannot be transferred without a theorem on these sparse circles and their endogenous R.

PASS requires a concrete theorem and a valid adapter whose total cost improves the present bound toward o(M3), including moving R, primitivity and all residual support types. If no such input exists, record that these candidate mechanisms are presently blocked; do not proceed to infinite case classification. No promise of closure within a few cards is warranted.

# M3-T11-154 — Global bridge audit: alphabet-cover cost, bilateral peeling and geometric height budget


STATUS=PROVED_CERTIFICATE_COST_BARRIER_AND_BILATERAL_DEGREE_FIREWALL
GLOBAL_BRIDGE_VERDICT=FAIL_FOR_TESTED_CERTIFICATES_NOT_IMPOSSIBILITY_OF_THE_TARGET
AUDIT_MODE=WITHIN_SESSION_PROOF_REDERIVATION_AND_EXACT_REPLAY_NOT_EXTERNAL
NEW_GLOBAL_OR_NEGLIGIBLE_SECTOR_BOUND=false
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
PRIMARY_GATE_STATUS=OPEN
NEXT=M3-T11-155 SameWitnessGlobalIncidenceBudget


## Starting authority and why154 is an audit


Fresh MAIN, INDEX, RESULT-LEDGER, active T11 ROUTE and the complete153 card all designate153 as latest.152's prescribed-alphabet sector and153's small-cofactor sector are retained. The unresolved population E_bal consists of original primitive canonical positive endpoints at exact R<=B with some prime outside S_B and with R/p^v_p(R)>Y_B for every p|R, where S_B is the first floor((log B)^(4/3)) split primes and Y_B=B^(1/3)/(1+log B)^30.


The user specifically asked whether repeated partial exclusions really lead to closure.154 tests that logical bridge. It does not add another negligible sector and does not claim a new global exponent. It proves a lower bound for a proposed NUMERICAL CERTIFICATE, distinguishes that from a lower bound on physical endpoints, and tests a genuine all-degree geometric theorem with the correct height.


## 1. The scalar balanced residual has nearly linear size


Let T tend to infinity, B=4T^2, and V_T be the primes p in [T,2T] with p=1 modulo4 that are outside S_B. Write v=|V_T|. The prime number theorem for progression1 modulo4 gives


 v ~ T/(2 log T),
 #{pq:p,q in V_T,p<q}=binom(v,2) asymp B/(log B)^2.   (154.1)


Removing at most |S_B|=O((log B)^(4/3)) primes does not change this asymptotic. Unique factorization makes the products distinct. Every such R=pq lies between B/4 and B; is odd and split; satisfies151's scalar conditions p<=3q^2 and q<=3p^2; lies outside the prescribed alphabet; and has both complementary factors p,q>=T>Y_B for large T.


These are SCALAR DIAGONAL CANDIDATES. None is asserted to support a physical cuboid or to pass all Gaussian witness conditions. The conclusion is that the displayed residual support inequalities themselves do not make the remaining candidate set small.


The external input is only the standard fixed-modulus prime number theorem, stated in the final paragraph of NIST DLMF27.11. The construction, residual checks and counting consequence here are derived in this card.


## 2. A rigorous lower bound on152's full alphabet-cover certificate


For a finite split-prime alphabet S, retain152's numerical cap


 U_S(B)=min(C0*K^|S|, inf_(sigma>0) W_S(B,sigma)),
 W_S=64 B^sigma product_(p in S) F(p^(-sigma)),
 F(x)=sum_(n>=0)(2n+1)^3 x^n,
 C0=48^36288, K=48^15552.


Put k=|S intersect V_T|. Then, for EVERY S,


 U_S(B) >= binom(k,2).                                (154.2)


Proof. Each pair of distinct primes from S intersect V_T gives R=pq<=B. Its term in the positive Euler expansion of W_S is64*(3*3)^3*(B/R)^sigma, at least1. Thus W_S>=binom(k,2) for every sigma, and its infimum has the same lower bound. Separately, C0*K^|S|>=2^|S|>=binom(|S|,2)>=binom(k,2), including the cases k<2. Taking the minimum preserves this lower bound.


Consequently, for ANY family F_B of alphabets covering EVERY scalar candidate pair from V_T,


 sum_(S in F_B) U_S(B)
 >= sum_(S in F_B) binom(|S intersect V_T|,2)
 >= binom(v,2) asymp B/(log B)^2.                     (154.3)


This is a lower bound on the particular upper-bound certificate proposed in152, not on P(B). It applies regardless of alphabet sizes, overlaps or how cleverly the alphabets are chosen. Therefore covering all of this scalar residual and then adding those existing numerical caps cannot certify o(B^(1/3)). It must first exploit PHYSICAL support thinning, or replace the caps by stronger joint arithmetic estimates. It is not enough to add more alphabets.


For the polylog-sized design |S|<=(log B)^A, an additional transparent family-cost bound is #F_B >> B/(log B)^(2+2A). This has polynomial exponent1, whereas152's sufficient covered-sector budget requires alpha+1-1/A<1/3. The exact certificate obstruction(154.3) is stronger and does not rely on using that sufficient budget.


## 3. Two-sided prime peeling: bounded fibers do not multiply


Test the same balanced two-prime window, now retaining actual cofactor witnesses. Fix q in V_T. Since Norm(G)=q^2 has12 Gaussian solutions, the labelled witness count in153 is


 3*12^2+12^3=2160.


For each nonzero C, Norm(C)<=9q^4<=144T^4. If T>12, three distinct candidate primes p in [T,2T] with p^2|Norm(C) would force Norm(C)>=T^6>144T^4. Thus at most TWO such p exist for a fixed witness. Here n=1. The constant-fiber reconstruction in153 consequently gives at most4320 encodings for fixed q, and


 P_two-prime-window(B) <=4320 v=O(B^(1/2)/log B).     (154.4)


This is an upper bound on physical endpoints in the specified window, not a new o(M3) sector theorem. It is still above the sufficient B^(1/3) scale. The reverse p-fixed count has the same bound.


Define a directed NECESSARY relation A(q,p): some two- or three-term Gaussian cofactor witness at q has C!=0 and p^2|Norm(C). Its out-degree in the window is at most4320. Physical pairs must lie in the mutual relation A(q,p) and A(p,q). The two existential witnesses need not reconstruct the SAME endpoint; that compatibility cannot be dropped and later treated as an independent saving.


There is a precise logical firewall: bounded degrees on both sides alone do not imply o(T^(2/3)) edges. A matching on v vertices has degree1 in both directions but floor(v/2) edges, asymptotically much larger than T^(2/3). This is an ABSTRACT countermodel to inference from degree bounds; it is NOT a claim that the arithmetic graph contains a matching of this size. Its actual norm-form correlations may yield a much stronger theorem. That is exactly the missing work.


One explicit shared-witness condition is available. For p^n,q^m||R and an index i that is a unit at both primes (such an index exists), the p-oriented and q-oriented reconstructions satisfy


 bar(pi_p)^(2n) G_i^(p)
   = bar(pi_q)^(2m) G_i^(q), or its complex conjugate. (154.5)


Their real parts are the SAME positive physical edge. This equality, the remaining coordinates and the exact sphere identity must be counted together. Two separate norm-divisor tests or two independently chosen witnesses do not supply(154.5). No correlation saving is proved here.


## 4. A genuine all-degree geometric bridge also misses the current budget


Consider the standard cuboid surface X in P^6 with coordinates (a,b,c,u,v,w,R) and equations


 u^2=a^2+b^2, v^2=a^2+c^2, w^2=b^2+c^2,
 R^2=a^2+b^2+c^2.


This is a geometrically integral complete-intersection surface of degree16. Here is the adapter rather than an unsupported degree claim. Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, the four squareclasses a^2+b^2, a^2+c^2, b^2+c^2, a^2+b^2+c^2 are independent in the projective base function field: each has a branch component occurring to odd order in it and in none of the other three. The four monic quadratic extensions therefore have generic degree16. The coordinate algebra is free of rank16 over the edge-coordinate algebra, hence embeds in this generic field and is integral. The four quadrics have codimension4; Bezout gives degree16. For a positive primitive endpoint the full integral tuple is primitive and its maximum coordinate is exactly R. Thus the project's cutoff is the projective height H<=B, with NO favorable rescaling.


Salberger, “Counting rational points on projective varieties”, Theorem0.9(b), supplies for a geometrically integral degree-d surface a collection of O(B^(3/(2sqrt(d))) log B+1) bounded-degree curves, outside which the point count is O(B^(3/sqrt(d)+o(1))). Applying it with d=16 gives


 number of covering curves: O(B^(3/8) log B+1),
 exceptional point budget: O(B^(3/4+o(1))).             (154.6)


Primary source: Salberger2023, Theorem0.9. The general, possibly singular surface theorem is used; the smooth P^3 theorem0.5 is NOT silently transferred to X. This is a quantitative coverage-plus-residual theorem of the type discussed in150, but its supplied exponents do not certify o(B^(1/3)). Even an optimistic constant occupancy per curve would leave the supplied curve-family budget above that scale, and the exceptional term independently remains too large. These are insufficient UPPER budgets, not lower bounds on the best possible cover or the true point count.


Raising the embedding degree is not a remedy. Under the k-th Veronese embedding, degree becomes16k^2 while the exact endpoint height becomes R^k. The two exponents after converting back to B are


 k*3/(2sqrt(16k^2))=3/8,
 k*3/sqrt(16k^2)=3/4.                                (154.7)


The degree formula is (kH)^2=k^2 H^2. The height equality follows because the Veronese coordinates include every pure k-th power; their gcd is1 for a primitive tuple, and the largest is R^k. This prevents artificial exponent credit from an embedding change.

# M3-T11-153 — Summed small-cofactor count with unrestricted moving primes


STATUS=PROVED_UNIFORM_MOVING_PRIME_SMALL_COFACTOR_COUNT

## Authority, population and the actual improvement


The live MAIN / INDEX / RESULT-LEDGER / active T11 ROUTE already designate152 as current authority.152 proves a negligible sector for ONE prescribed prime alphabet, but leaves the moving-prime complement unbounded.153 uses151's exact Gaussian valuation identity to SUM a different sector, allowing the exceptional prime to range over ALL split primes. No restriction on curve degree, genus, prime-support alphabet, or coefficient packet is introduced.


P(B) counts the original primitive canonical positive physical endpoints at exact R<=B. As in151, use positive integer edges e1,e2,e3, complementary face diagonals f1,f2,f3, gcd(e1,e2,e3)=1, ei^2+fi^2=R^2, and sum ei^2=R^2. Original canonical masks remain in force; dropping masks is used only for an upper bound. R is odd and all its primes split in Z[i]. One endpoint is one count, using the endpoint-to-edge-triple injection retained in151.


For B>=2 and 1<=Y<=B, let N(B,Y) count endpoints for which SOME prime power p^n exactly dividing R has complementary factor m=R/p^n<=Y. This is a union over all primes and all valuations, not a fixed-prime statement.


THEOREM:


 N(B,Y) <= 512 Y (1+log Y)^27 (1+log B).                 (153.1)


The constant512 is deliberately nonoptimal. Thus N(B,B^theta)<=B^(theta+o(1)) for any fixed0<theta<1. In particular theta<1/3 gives o(M3(B)) from retained M3(B)>>B^(1/3).


More sharply, put L=1+log B and Y_B=B^(1/3)/L^30. For sufficiently large B so Y_B>=1,


 N(B,Y_B) <= 512 B^(1/3)/L^2 = o(M3(B)).                 (153.2)


This counts moving primes and all their exponents at a nearly B^(1/3) complementary-factor threshold. It does NOT bound all endpoints or the entire complement of152.


## 1. Prime discovery from the cofactor witnesses


Fix an endpoint and a prime p^n exactly dividing R; put m=R/p^n. Choose one deterministic Gaussian prime pi above p. For each edge not divisible by p, independently change the sign of its complementary diagonal so that


 H_i=e_i+i f_i=bar(pi)^(2n) G_i,   Norm(G_i)=m^2.


These conjugations leave the positive edges unchanged. Let I={i:p does not divide e_i}; primitivity and the sphere equation give r=|I| in {2,3}. Write C=sum_(i in I)G_i^2.151 proves, directly from the exact sphere identity,


 C != 0,   pi^2 divides C,   Norm(C)<=r^2 m^4<=9m^4.    (153.3)


For completeness: the terms of sum H_i^2+sum bar(H_i)^2+2R^2=0 outside bar(pi)^(4n)C are all divisible by pi^2. If r=3 and C=0 the identity contradicts R>0; if r=2 and C=0 it reduces to4e_j^2=0 for the remaining edge. Positivity rules this out. Each |G_i^2|=m^2 gives the norm bound. No independence of prime orientations is assumed.


Crucially, for FIXED m,I,(G_i), the nonzero integer Norm(C) is already fixed BEFORE p is chosen. Every permissible p satisfies p^2|Norm(C), p>=5, and p does not divide m. There are at most


 log(9m^4)/(2 log5)


such distinct primes. The smaller Gaussian condition pi^2|C may safely be discarded for this upper bound. A fixed cofactor therefore pays O(log m) prime choices, even though the primes move globally. A bound p<=3m^2 alone would not have this property.


## 2. Reconstruction prevents an extra physical fiber cost


Let A(m)=#{G in Z[i]:Norm(G)=m^2}=4D(m), with D(m)=product_(q^a||m)(2a+1), for the split m that occur here. The witness count for fixed m is


 3A(m)^2+A(m)^3 <= 112 D(m)^3.                         (153.4)


The factor3 is the choice of the two-element set I. The three-element case has one I. Units and all Gaussian allocations are already included in A(m). Tuples with C=0 are discarded, since no positive endpoint maps to them.


Given m,I,(G_i),p,n, the chosen pi determines H_i=bar(pi)^(2n)G_i for i in I. Their real parts determine those edges. If r=3 all edges are known. If r=2 the remaining POSITIVE edge is uniquely determined, if it exists, by


 e_j=+sqrt(R^2-sum_(i in I)e_i^2).


Reject nonsquares, zero or negative edges, wrong p-divisibility, nonprimitive triples and failed face-diagonal/canonical masks. The remaining face diagonals are then fixed in the original sign convention. There is at most ONE original endpoint for this complete witness. No factor R^o(1), extra curve-family count, or uncontrolled inverse multiplicity is needed.


Each physical endpoint in N(B,Y) is encoded at least once. One can choose its least qualifying p to obtain a deterministic injection. The enumeration may contain several encodings of an endpoint, which is harmless in an upper bound. It is not necessary to charge the number of possible qualifying primes a second time.


For each fixed p and m, n>=1 and mp^n<=B allow at most log B/log5 choices. This explicitly sums all valuations, including the r=2 branch where151 did not bound p^n by3m^2.


## 3. Sum all complementary factors, with explicit logarithmic cost


Combining the preceding steps gives


 N(B,Y) <= [112/(2(log5)^2)] log B
             * sum_(m<=Y) D(m)^3 log(9m^4).             (153.5)


Extending the m-sum to all positive integers is safe. Let tau_27 be the27-fold divisor function. Locally,


 (2a+1)^3 <= binom(a+26,26), hence D(m)^3<=tau_27(m).


Proof of the local inequality: equality holds at a=0. The ratio comparison follows from


 (2a+1)^3(a+27)-(2a+3)^3(a+1)
 =184a^3+240a^2+82a >=0.


The elementary ordered-factor count gives


 sum_(m<=Y) tau_27(m)
 <= Y (sum_(a<=Y)1/a)^26 <= Y(1+log Y)^26.


Indeed, fix the first26 positive factors and bound the number of last factors by Y divided by their product; enlarging each of the26 sums to a<=Y is an upper bound. Since log(9m^4)<=4(1+log Y), (153.5) implies(153.1), with room in the displayed constant512. No prime number theorem, deep unit-equation theorem, probabilistic sieve, or hypothesis on the actual prime sizes is used in this summed estimate.


## 4. Exact new residual after combining152 and153


Keep152's prescribed S_B: the first floor((log B)^(4/3)) primes1 modulo4. Let E_small have supp(R) contained in S_B. Define E_peel to contain endpoints OUTSIDE E_small with some p^n||R and R/p^n<=Y_B. Define E_bal to contain the remaining endpoints. Then, on the original physical measure,


 E(B)=E_small disjoint-union E_peel disjoint-union E_bal,
 P_small(B)=o(M3(B)),
 P_peel(B)<=N(B,Y_B)=o(M3(B)).                         (153.6)


Thus P(B)/M3(B)->0 is equivalent to P_bal(B)/M3(B)->0. Every endpoint still requiring a bound has BOTH:


 (a) some prime divisor of R outside S_B;
 (b) R/p^v_p(R)>Y_B for EVERY prime p dividing R.


Equivalently, every full prime-power divisor is <R/Y_B. This is only a necessary support description of the unresolved mass. Do not confuse a bound involving B with a dyadic statement involving the actual R. The result counts actual endpoints in the removed sectors; it does not claim the surviving diagonal set has few integers.


On a dyadic top shell B/2<R<=B, the small-cofactor sector at Y_B cannot have r=3 for large B, since151 would force R<=3m^3<=3B/L^90. Nor can it have n=1, since p<=3m^2 gives the same contradiction. Thus the new top-shell count acts on the r=2, repeated-prime-power branch; do not market it as disposing of all large squarefree prime divisors. Both branches were correctly included in the uniform theorem.

The new summed estimate therefore does not contradict151's candidate-support lower bound; most relaxed candidates may never pass this correlated witness condition.

# M3-T11-151 — Integer-wide dominant-prime exclusion and quantitative marginal-support barrier


STATUS=ALL_ENDPOINT_NECESSARY_CONDITION_PROVED_MARGINAL_COUNTING_BRIDGE_REJECTED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
PRIMARY_GATE_STATUS=OPEN
TI=PARKED
CURRENT_ATTACK=JointGaussianSupportCorrelationUnderExactR

## Authority and population


Fresh MAIN / INDEX / RESULT-LEDGER / active T11 ROUTE and research-card150 are the authority.150 stopped degree-by-degree curve escalation. This card works directly with every original primitive physical integer endpoint, including points outside the rational curves studied in147–149. No carrier assignment, parameter degree, genus restriction, or polynomial-root-pair interpretation of an integer R is used.


Write positive edges e1,e2,e3, complementary face diagonals f1,f2,f3, and the integer space diagonal R, with gcd(e1,e2,e3)=1, ei^2+fi^2=R^2 and sum ei^2=R^2. Exact cutoff is R<=B. Canonical endpoint masks remain in force; enlarging to these equations is safe only for an upper bound. Retained138/141 ensure R odd and the edge/R contents are pairwise coprime. Every prime dividing R is 1 modulo4: an inert prime dividing ei^2+fi^2 forces it to divide every ei, contradicting primitivity. This elementary argument is included here as a dependency, not claimed as historical novelty.


## 1. Global arithmetic theorem


For EACH prime power p^n exactly dividing R, put m=R/p^n. Then every such endpoint satisfies


 p <= 3 m^2.                                             (151.1)


There are stronger branch conditions. Let r be the number of edges not divisible by p. Then r is2 or3. If r=2, p<=2m^2. If r=3, p^n<=3m^2. In particular, a primitive positive endpoint cannot have R equal to a power of a single prime. This is a theorem about actual integer endpoints, uniform in height and in all possible geometric complexity; it is not an application of149's curve-polynomial theorem.


Proof in Z[i]. Choose p=pi*bar(pi), Norm(pi)=p. Independently conjugate Hi=ei+i fi so v_pi(Hi)<=v_bar(pi)(Hi); this changes only the sign of fi. Norm(Hi)=R^2. For an edge not divisible by p, v_pi(Hi)=0 and v_bar(pi)(Hi)=2n, hence
 Hi=bar(pi)^(2n) Gi,  Gi in Z[i], Norm(Gi)=m^2.
At least two edges are not divisible by p: if two edges are divisible by p, sum ei^2=R^2 forces the third to be divisible by p as well. Let I be the set of these r edges and C=sum_(i in I) Gi^2.


The exact sphere identity is
 sum Hi^2 + sum bar(Hi)^2 + 2R^2 = 0.                    (151.2)
All terms outside bar(pi)^(4n) C are divisible by pi^2. Indeed, a remaining edge divisible by p has both Gaussian valuations at least1; the conjugates of the I-terms have valuation4n; and R^2 has valuation2n. Thus pi^2 divides C. If r=3, there is no remaining edge, and the conjugate terms have valuation4n while 2R^2 has valuation exactly2n. Consequently v_pi(C)=2n.


C is nonzero. For r=3, C=0 would make both entire sums of squares in(151.2) zero, contradicting R>0. For r=2, C=0 gives H1^2+H2^2=0 and its conjugate;(151.2) then reduces to4e3^2=0, contradicting positivity. Finally |Gi^2|=m^2, so Norm(C)<=r^2 m^4. A nonzero Gaussian integer divisible by pi^2 has norm at least p^2; in the r=3 case it has norm at least p^(2n). These yield the stated inequalities. Units are absorbed into Gi; no complex phase cancellation is assumed absent.


Thus all original endpoints lie in the explicit diagonal support
 S(B)={odd R<=B: all p|R are1 mod4, and p<=3(R/p^v_p(R))^2 for every p|R}.
The excluded diagonal part has EXACTLY ZERO physical endpoints; all remaining endpoint mass is on S(B). This is an exact global support reduction, not a curve/residual covering conjecture. It supplies no bound on the mass remaining there.


## 2. Quantitative test: this marginal condition cannot itself reach the certified scale


Do not embark on an unlimited sequence of additional scalar prime tests without testing their surviving support. The set S(B) already has


 #S(B) >> B^(2/3)/log B.                                (151.3)


Explicit proof. For every prime q=1 mod4, q>5, choose the least k>=0 with 3*5^(2k)>=q and set R(q)=5^k q. Both prime divisors are split. For p=q the support condition holds by construction; for p=5 it holds because 5<=3q^2. Moreover this family even passes the stronger inequalities p^n<=3m^2 at BOTH prime divisors: q<=3*5^(2k), and 5^k<5 sqrt(q/3)<=3q^2. Minimality gives R(q)<(5/sqrt(3))*q^(3/2). Distinct q give distinct R(q). Taking q<=((sqrt(3)/5)B)^(2/3) and applying the prime number theorem in progression1 modulo4 proves(151.3).


External theorem used only for this obstruction's quantitative size: NIST DLMF section27.11, final paragraph, https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.11 (accessed in this session), states pi(x;k,h)~x/(phi(k)log x) for coprime h,k. The construction and its support inequalities are derived here. These R(q) are NOT asserted to support physical cuboids. They are counterexamples to deducing an o(B^(1/3)) DIAGONAL-CANDIDATE bound from(151.1), even if the stronger branch inequalities are imposed without joint edge data.


Therefore the dominant-prime sieve is useful as a zero-mass exclusion, but is FAIL as a standalone route to the sufficient o(B^(1/3)) endpoint scale. This does not prove that o(M3(B)) is impossible, nor rule out combining this condition with other correlated constraints. It rules out assigning global-counting credit to this condition alone.


## 3. Exact remaining joint receiver and counting costs


Let H(R)={H in Z[i]: Norm(H)=R^2}. For split R, unique factorization gives
 #H(R)=4 product_(p^n||R)(2n+1).
Each signed triple H1,H2,H3 with real parts e1,e2,e3 satisfies the sphere condition exactly when(151.2) holds. For each R define J(R) to count such triples with nonzero real and imaginary parts, primitive real parts, and the original physical/canonical masks retained or explicitly enlarged. Choose a deterministic positive sign convention and edge order for an injection from canonical physical endpoints into the triples; discarded masks only enlarge J. Then
 P(B) <= sum_(R in S(B)) J(R).
There is no uncounted geometric residual: every physical endpoint has its three complementary face diagonals and hence a triple. No packet constants or curve-family costs have been hidden. The crude bound J(R)<=#H(R)^3=R^o(1) only gives B^(1+o(1)); it has NO global exponent credit.


The load-bearing task is the averaged EXACT joint identity(151.2), not the separate marginal divisibilities pi^2|C, the number of allowable R, or a fixed-R representation bound. The same Hi must work at every prime and satisfy the archimedean equality; treating local choices as independent would discard the essential correlation. Content/prime orientation choices depend on the edge, and must be charged in any enlarged count.


## 4. Decision, scope and restart


151 proves an all-endpoint arithmetic exclusion and proves quantitatively that its scalar support relaxation is too large for the certified sufficient scale. It does NOT meet150's acceptance criterion for aggregate exponent improvement. GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT remains0; the gate remainsOPEN. The theorem is a valid uniform link from the original population to explicit arithmetic support, with zero excluded mass, but should not be marketed as closure progress in the endpoint sum.


Next152: attempt a uniform averaged bound for the correlated Gaussian triple identity above, including the growing prime-factor/valuation allocation cost under exactR. A claimed improvement must bound the complete sum or a specified part AND its complement. First dedupe against the existing Gaussian/root-packet and charged cofactor routes; do not rename their fixed-block estimates. If no summed saving follows, record that obstruction promptly rather than enumerating degrees or local prime-factor cases.147–149 remain retained and curve escalation remains paused. TI parked;120 retracted.

## 3. Two quantifier gaps that must not recur


First, the number of conjugate root pairs in149 refers to the polynomial R(s,t) of a selected parameterized curve. An individual endpoint only has an integer space diagonal R. It has no intrinsic polynomial-root-pair count. Therefore149 does NOT by itself partition the endpoint population into <=2-root-pair and >=3-root-pair points. Such a partition would require a proved carrier assignment, overlap handling and family cost; it cannot be inferred from terminology.


Second, even eliminating every nonconstant P1_Q curve would not automatically eliminate or count the remaining rational points. A constant map at any rational endpoint is outside the nonconstant theorem, and endpoints need not lie on a proved P1_Q family. Excluding rational curves is not a residual rational-point estimate.


A simple logical countermodel for exchanging limits: place normalized mass1 entirely at degree d(B)=floor(log2 B). For each fixed d the mass eventually becomes0, yet the all-degree sum stays1. This is NOT a physical cuboid counterexample; it shows why fixed-degree negligibility alone cannot justify a growing-degree/global inference. The historical firewall already forbids that inference.

 P(B)=P_car(B)+P_res(B),
 P_car(B)<=sum_(C in F_B) N_C(B),
where N_C counts the original endpoints, including source/content/packet masks and exactR. Overlap is safe for an upper union bound; a claimed equality or saving needs explicit charging. Closure requires a proved bound for the SUM and a proved residual bound. A carrier degree/coefficient parameter is allowed only with a proved physical-height adapter and summable cost.


Historical budget illustration remains conditional: if the retained degree6 per-carrier B^(1/6+o(1)) bound is UNIFORM in a growing family and its constants are controlled, a family number B^(1/6-delta) suffices for carrier mass B^(1/3-delta+o(1)). # M3-T11-149 — Two-pair obstruction in all degrees; square-free sextic phase receiver


STATUS=PROVED_ALL_DEGREE_TWO_CONJUGATE_PAIR_OBSTRUCTION_AND_EXACT_SEXTIC_RECEIVER
AUDIT_MODE=WITHIN_SESSION_REDERIVATION_AND_EXACT_CHECKS_NOT_EXTERNAL

NEXT=M3-T11-150 SquareFreeDegreeSixPhaseCompatibilityOrDirectSupportEstimate


Authority: fresh MAIN / INDEX / RESULT-LEDGER / active ROUTE all148; latest148 standalone research-card and audit read.146 unique degree-preserving lift and147 no-real-zero lemma are retained.148 already excludes one-pair powers in all degrees and the simple two-pair quartic. This card handles arbitrary two-pair multiplicities and gives a concrete receiver for the remaining degree6 case. Do not reread the known history from the beginning.


## 1. Scope, dedupe and result


Use the common degree d of a homogeneous basepoint-free P1_Q parameter map in the138/139 plus projection, with common factors removed. A contained generically open map has, by146, real/rational forms E_i,F_i,R of that same degree satisfying
 E_i^2+F_i^2=R^2, sum E_i^2=R^2.
Their common basepoints are absent. A real zero of R is impossible by147. Original positivity/source/packet/coefficient/orientation/cyclic/content/canonical conditions remain necessary.


We prove that if the complex roots of R occupy at most TWO distinct conjugate pairs, EVERY nonconstant basepoint-free signed lift has an identically zero edge, for arbitrary multiplicities and arbitrary degree. The one-pair case was already148; the new part is two pairs when at least one multiplicity>=2. Together with148's simple two-pair quartic, this excludes the entire two-pair class.


Consequently any nonconstant potentially all-positive contained degree6 P1_Q map must have square-free R with THREE distinct conjugate root pairs. This remaining class is OPEN; existence and nonexistence are not proved. Historical Stage19 M4/odd-M absence and Stage20 Saunderson M6 remain as recorded in M3-HIST28-GEOMETRY-FW-001. No comparison with the current parameter degree or Stage19 M6 absence is claimed. No global counting credit is added.


## 2. Elementary sparse-power zero-multiplicity lemma


Let S(w)=sum_(j=1)^r d_j*w^(ell_j), with nonzero d_j, distinct integer ell_j, r<=3. At any finite w_0!=0, a nonzero S has zero multiplicity at most r-1. Indeed vanishing to order>=r implies its first r Euler derivatives (w*d/dw)^h, h=0..r-1, vanish. Their coefficient matrix is (ell_j^h*w_0^(ell_j)). Its determinant is product w_0^(ell_j) times the nonzero Vandermonde product_(i<j)(ell_j-ell_i). This forces every d_j=0, a contradiction. Negative exponents are allowed because w_0 is nonzero. Equal exponents are grouped first; cancellations can reduce the number of terms or make S identically zero. This is a universal lemma, not a finite exponent search.


## 3. Exhaustive two-pair factor allocations


Suppose R=Q_1^n*Q_2^m up to a real scalar, with distinct definite quadratics, n,m>=1. Use148's real projective normalization, valid also with multiplicities, to write
 R=(L*bar(L))^n*(M*bar(M))^m,
 z=L/bar(L), w=M/bar(M).
Every H_i=E_i+iF_i has
 H_i/R=c_i*z^(a_i)*w^(b_i),
 |c_i|=1, -n<=a_i<=n, -m<=b_i<=m.
This follows exactly from unique factorization of H_i*bar(H_i)=R^2 and conjugation, not a chosen family. If |a_i|<n for all three coordinates, each H_i and bar(H_i), hence all E_i,F_i and R, is divisible by Q_1. This contradicts basepoint-freeness. Thus at least one |a_i|=n.


When one multiplicity is>=2, choose that pair as Q_1, so n>=2. Independently conjugate H_i if needed to arrange a_i>=0; this changes F_i's sign but leaves E_i and every squared identity unchanged. We use this only for the proof, not to relax original signed masks. Let t_0 be the simple pole of z. Since the two root pairs are distinct, w(t_0) is finite and nonzero and w is unramified there. Write r for the number of coordinates with a_i=n, so r=1,2 or3.


## 4. Pole order forces a boundary edge


The sphere identity is
 sum_i [c_i^2*z^(2a_i)*w^(2b_i) + bar(c_i)^2*z^(-2a_i)*w^(-2b_i)] +2=0.


If r=1, its sole leading term has a pole of order2n at t_0 with a nonzero coefficient. All other terms have pole order at most2n-2, or are regular. Cancellation is impossible.


If r=2, factor their pole part as z^(2n)*S(w), where S has at most two powers. Every other term has pole order<=2n-2. Thus S must vanish to order>=2 at w(t_0). Section2 forces S identically zero. Since the two coefficients are nonzero, their exponents must coincide, b_1=b_2, and c_1^2+c_2^2=0. Their conjugate terms cancel identically as well. Therefore E_1^2+E_2^2=R^2, and the original sphere identity forces E_3^2=0: E_3 is identically zero. Relabeling coordinates is harmless.


If r=3, all three positive-pole terms are z^(2n)*S(w), with at most three distinct powers after grouping. The reflected terms are regular (indeed vanish) at t_0, so S must have zero multiplicity>=2n>=4. Section2 permits at most2 for a nonzero S. Hence S is identically zero. Its reflected conjugate sum also vanishes identically, leaving the impossible constant identity2=0.


The cases are exhaustive. Thus arbitrary two-pair multiplicities with at least one>=2 force a zero edge. The remaining n=m=1 case is exactly148 and already has the same conclusion. This establishes the all-degree two-pair obstruction. Legitimate zero-edge boundary maps are preserved; constant maps are also not excluded as perfect-cuboid candidates. The theorem concerns nonconstant maps with no common factor/basepoint.


## 5. Remaining square-free degree6: finite allocation and exact phase receiver


For degree6, the other partitions of root multiplicity are3 and2+1, already excluded by148 and sections3–4. The only remaining possibility is1+1+1. Normalize two upper roots to i,ki with k>0,k!=1 and write the third as u+iv with v>0, distinct from the first two. Then
 R=(t^2+1)(t^2+k^2)((t-u)^2+v^2).
Let alpha=(i,ki,u+iv). For a=(a_1,a_2,a_3) in {-1,0,1}^3 define
 H_a=product_j (t-alpha_j)^(1+a_j)*(t-bar(alpha_j))^(1-a_j), C_a=H_a^2.
There are exactly27 allocations, H_a*bar(H_a)=R^2 and C_-a=bar(C_a), degree12. Every coordinate H_i=c_i H_(a_i), |c_i|=1.


At each root pair j, zero active allocations (all a_ij=0) would make all forms divisible by Q_j. Exactly one active allocation gives an uncancellable order2 pole in the sphere identity, after orienting that coordinate toward the pole. Therefore each column of the3x3 allocation matrix has at least TWO nonzero entries. There are20 possible signed columns, hence20^3=8000 ordered allocation matrices satisfying this necessary local condition, versus27^3=19683 unrestricted ordered triples. This is a finite algebraic pattern reduction, NOT a count of Stage37 endpoints or a proof all8000 survive.


For a fixed allowed allocation triple and fixed real root parameters, write lambda_i=c_i^2=x_i+i*y_i. The FULL signed sphere identity is exactly the following13 real linear coefficient equations plus three unit-circle constraints:
 sum_i [x_i*Re(C_(a_i)) - y_i*Im(C_(a_i))] + R^2 =0,
 x_i^2+y_i^2=1, i=1,2,3.
Equate coefficients of t^h for h=0..12; homogenization includes infinity. Thus a13x6 real linear system with right-hand side -coeff(R^2), intersected with three unit circles, is an exact REAL-lift receiver. Every unit lambda_i has a unit square root c_i, which reconstructs E_i=Re(c_i H_(a_i)), F_i=Im(c_i H_(a_i)); conversely every real polynomial lift gives this system. Basepoint-freeness still must hold, and original endpoint positivity/masks must be checked separately. In the square-free setting the >=2-active condition already guarantees no common signed basepoint at roots of R; elsewhere R is nonzero. This does NOT prove rationality of the reconstructed coefficients: Q descent is a separate unresolved requirement, especially when roots are not individually defined over Q(i).


This receiver accounts for the dependence of all phase functions on one parameter; it never treats three phases as independent Laurent variables. It replaces an unsigned slice or genus observation by the exact original full signed equations.


## 6. Why148's circuit shortcut does not transfer


In degree4, nine squared allocations had a rank8 one-dimensional relation, necessarily involving all eight nonconstant modes. For degree6 there are27 squared allocations in a13-dimensional polynomial coefficient space, so the full relation space always has dimension AT LEAST14. A one-dimensional all-mode circuit is impossible. Exact examples with roots (i,2i,1+i) and (i,3i,2+i) both have rank13 and relation dimension14. These are fixed-root examples, not a universal rank formula or an exclusion theorem. A relation supported on at most six allocation modes plus the center must now be checked using the13x6 receiver and its phase norms; the quartic sparse-support argument cannot simply be repeated.

This is occupancy per map, not a global curve-cover bound. A contained generically open degree6 map must have square-free three-pair R; this class is not closed. # M3-T11-148 — Full signed quartic parameter obstruction and single-pair power firewall


STATUS=PROVED_FULL_SIGNED_DEGREE4_PARAMETER_OBSTRUCTION
AUDIT_MODE=WITHIN_SESSION_EXACT_ALGEBRA_CERTIFICATE_NOT_EXTERNAL
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
PRIMARY_GATE_STATUS=OPEN
TI=PARKED
NEXT=M3-T11-149 DegreeSixFullSignedAllocationOrDirectSupportEstimate


Authority: freshly read MAIN / INDEX / RESULT-LEDGER / active ROUTE all147; standalone147 card/audit read. Use146's degree-preserving unique polynomial lift on the generic138/139 open mask and147's real basepoint obstruction. Preserve original endpoint masks, retracted120 and parked TI. No full-history reread.


## 1. Scope and dedupe


The degree here is the common degree d of a homogeneous basepoint-free P1_Q parameter map into the138/139 plus coordinates [A_1:A_2:A_3:R], after common factors are removed. It is not automatically the degree of its image, genus or the historical K3 quasi-polarization M-degree. Historical M3-HIST28-GEOMETRY-FW-001 already records Stage19 physical M4 and odd-M absence, Stage20 Saunderson M6, and no proved Stage19 M6 absence. Keep those facts and do not count their rediscovery as new credit. We still have no comparison identifying M-degree with this projection parameter degree. This card supplies a direct146 receiver and exact factor-allocation certificate, rather than a new global low-degree spectrum.


We prove: a nonconstant basepoint-free degree4 real polynomial lift satisfying
 E_i^2+F_i^2=R^2, sum_i E_i^2=R^2
cannot have all three E_i strictly positive at any real parameter. In fact at least one E_i is identically zero. Thus a contained generically open degree4 P1_Q parameter map in P=0 has no eligible positive endpoints, by146. Constant positive rational lifts are NOT excluded; one would already be a perfect cuboid. Curves of positive genus, nonsplit normalization and isolated singular rational points are not covered by this theorem.


## 2. Single conjugate root pair: exclusion for every power


By147, R has no real projective zero. Suppose R is proportional to Q^n with Q a definite real quadratic. Normalize R=(L*bar(L))^n. Put H_i=E_i+iF_i. Unique factorization of H_i*bar(H_i)=R^2 gives
 H_i=c_i L^(n+k_i) bar(L)^(n-k_i), -n<=k_i<=n, |c_i|=1.
Hence H_i/R=c_i z^k_i, z=L/bar(L), and E_i/R=(c_i z^k_i+bar(c_i)z^(-k_i))/2. For k_i=0 this is a fixed real ratio a_i; otherwise the square has constant coefficient1/2. The nonconstant z makes Laurent coefficients independent. The sphere identity forces
 m/2+sum_fixed a_i^2=1,
where m is the number of nonzero k_i, and cancellation of every nonzero frequency. m=1 is impossible; m=3 has constant coefficient3/2. If m=2, their absolute frequencies must agree, their squared phases cancel, and the sole fixed a_i=0. If m=0 the image is constant and all forms share R. Thus every nonconstant single-pair-power lift has a zero edge, for ALL n. In particular the repeated-quadratic quartic case R=Q^2 is excluded physically. Boundary maps remain: take E_1+iE_2=(t-i)^(2n), E_3=0 and R=(t^2+1)^n.


## 3. Distinct pairs: real normalization and nine exhaustive allocations


The remaining real quartic with no real zero has two distinct conjugate pairs. A real projective change of parameter sends their upper half-plane roots to i and k*i, with k>0 and k!=1. For completeness: first send the first root to i by translation/scaling. For a second root p+iq, q>0, a transformation (cos(theta)z+sin(theta))/(-sin(theta)z+cos(theta)) fixes i; the numerator of its real part is p*cos(2theta)+(1-p^2-q^2)*sin(2theta)/2. Choose theta making this zero. Its denominator cannot vanish in the upper half-plane, and injectivity prevents k=1 for distinct roots. This is a real change; losing rational coefficients causes no issue for a real impossibility theorem.


Absorb a nonzero real scalar into all forms and normalize
 R=(t^2+1)(t^2+k^2).
The homogeneous statement includes infinity. For a,b in {-1,0,1}, define degree4 forms (dehomogenized below)
 H_ab=(t-i)^(1+a)(t+i)^(1-a)(t-ki)^(1+b)(t+ki)^(1-b).
Conjugation gives bar(H_ab)=H_(-a,-b), H_ab*bar(H_ab)=R^2. Every H_i=E_i+iF_i is exactly c_i H_(a_i,b_i), |c_i|=1. At each conjugate pair the exponents sum2, by H_i*bar(H_i)=R^2, so these nine allocations are exhaustive, not an ansatz. Put C_ab=H_ab^2, degree8, and C_00=R^2.


## 4. Exact rank8 circuit of the nine squared allocations


The nine C_ab have a one-dimensional relation space. Its generator has weights
 w_00=4(k^4-10k^2+1),
 w_a0=w_0b=-2(k^2-1)^2 for a,b nonzero,
 w_ab=(k-1)^4 for ab=1,
 w_ab=(k+1)^4 for ab=-1.
Then sum_(a,b) w_ab C_ab=0. Every one of the EIGHT off-center weights is nonzero for k>0,k!=1; the center weight may vanish, and we do NOT assume otherwise.


Here is a reproducible universal rank certificate, not a finite parameter census. Choose representatives (1,1),(1,0),(1,-1),(0,1). Write B_j=Im(C_rep_j) and T_j=Re(C_rep_j); these are odd and even polynomials respectively. In the odd coefficient rows t,t^3,t^5,t^7, the determinant of the four B columns is
 -32768*k^6*(k^2-1)^2.
In the even rows t^2,t^4,t^6,t^8, the determinant of columns T_1,T_2,T_3,R^2 is
 -2048*k^3*(k^2-1)^3.
Both are nonzero on the stated range. Odd and even coefficient subspaces are disjoint, so rank is at least8; the displayed relation makes it at most8. Passing between conjugate pairs and their real/imaginary parts is invertible over C. Thus the relation space is exactly one-dimensional.


verify148.py proves these determinant formulas by exact Gaussian rational arithmetic and interpolation: every matrix entry is a polynomial in k of degree<=4; a4x4 determinant has degree<=16. Its exact values at17 distinct integers determine it uniquely, and the interpolated coefficients equal the displayed polynomial coefficients. The relation coefficients have degree<=4 and C coefficients degree<=4, so their sum has degree<=8; exact zeros at17 distinct integers certify the identity coefficient by coefficient (nine coefficient rows). This is a finite certificate of polynomial identities with an explicit degree bound, not empirical extrapolation. Degenerate test nodes k=0,1 are allowed for polynomial certification; they are excluded from the rank theorem.


## 5. Sparse three-coordinate identity forces a boundary edge


Since E_i=(H_i+bar(H_i))/2 and H_i*bar(H_i)=R^2, the sphere identity is precisely
 sum_i (c_i^2 C_(a_i,b_i)+bar(c_i)^2 C_(-a_i,-b_i)) + 2 C_00 =0.
Three coordinates contribute at most SIX distinct off-center allocation modes. Consequently the resulting coefficient vector omits at least two off-center entries. By section4, any nonzero relation must have all eight off-center entries nonzero. Our coefficient vector must therefore be ZERO entry by entry.


Call (a,b)=(0,0) fixed, and group nonfixed modes into opposite pairs. A single coordinate in an opposite-pair group contributes a nonzero squared phase, so it cannot cancel. If two of the three coordinates rotate, they must lie in the SAME opposite-pair group and their squared phases cancel; the fixed coordinate c has center equation2+2 Re(c^2)=0. Since |c|=1, c=+/-i and its E is identically zero. If all three rotate, the center coefficient is2, impossible, even if all are in one group. One rotating coordinate is impossible. With zero rotating coordinates all forms are proportional to R and the projective image is constant/common-factor. This exhausts every allocation and proves the theorem. Surviving two-rotating boundary maps are algebraically valid; positivity removes them.


The two phase functions z=(t-i)/(t+i),w=(t-ki)/(t+ki) are algebraically dependent. Treating them as independent Laurent variables would be invalid. The rank8 circuit explicitly accounts for this dependence. Its center coefficient can vanish without weakening the sparse-support obstruction.


## 6. Projection receiver, counts and limits


For a degree4 basepoint-free Q parameter map contained in P=0 with generic146 open mask,146 supplies a polynomial signed lift of the same degree and no common basepoint. Sections2–5 exclude all-positive endpoints. If the open mask fails identically, it cannot contain an original eligible positive rational endpoint, by146's mask inclusion. A NONCONTAINED degree4 parameter map has a nonzero homogeneous degree64 pullback of P, so at most64 projective parameter roots and, by146 uniqueness, at most64 eligible endpoints. This includes infinity and does not assert a bound on the number/cost of such maps.


Together with147's odd-degree and degree2 obstructions, the first remaining possible nonconstant contained P1_Q parameter degree is6. Existence at degree6 is not proved, and no assertion is made about historical Stage19 M6. Smooth elliptic cubics, positive-genus quartics, rational curves whose normalization has no Q parameterization and isolated singular rational points are not silently removed. No global population estimate, exponent saving or perfect-cuboid nonexistence follows.

# M3-T11-147 — Degree-two and odd-parameter obstruction in the full signed projection


STATUS=PROVED_LOW_PARAMETER_DEGREE_ADAPTER_WITH_BOUNDARY_CLASSIFICATION
AUDIT_MODE=WITHIN_SESSION_ADVERSARIAL_REDERIVATION_NOT_EXTERNAL
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
PRIMARY_GATE_STATUS=OPEN

Authority: fresh MAIN / INDEX / RESULT-LEDGER / active ROUTE all146; latest146 card and audit read. Use146's full139 eliminant and degree-preserving unique inverse, with original138 positive endpoint masks retained. T11-120 remains retracted. No full-history reread.


## 1. Historical dedupe and exact scope


The current ledger already records M3-HIST28-GEOMETRY-FW-001: on the earlier blow-up/K3 models with quasi-polarization M, Stage19 physical M-degree4 rational curves and every odd physical M-degree are absent; Stage20 has the Saunderson M-degree6 curve. Stage19 M-degree6 absence is NOT proved. Those historical results remain authority and receive no new credit here. We have NOT identified that M-degree with the parameter degree in the138/139 plus projection. The contribution here is an explicit positivity proof in the146 lift coordinates, its degree-preserving projection receiver, and bounded noncontained-conic occupancy. It is not a claim of a new global low-degree spectrum or of Stage19 M-degree6 absence.


Parameter degree d below means the common degree of a homogeneous basepoint-free map from P1_Q to [A_1:A_2:A_3:R], after removing common factors. It does not mean genus, the earlier M-degree, or the degree of an arbitrary multiply-covered image. Real coefficients suffice for the obstruction. Constant maps are explicitly excluded from the nonconstant conclusion.


## 2. Pass from projection to a basepoint-free signed polynomial lift


Suppose the map is contained in P=0, and the146 open mask R*product(A_i*q_i*K_i) is not identically zero, where q_i=2R^2-A_i^2 and K_i=R^2-A_i^2. By146 over Q(t), there is a unique Y_i in Q(t) with Y_i^2=q_i and sum A_iY_i=-R^2. A rational function whose square is a polynomial is a polynomial (reduce numerator and denominator in the UFD Q[t]). Its degree is at most d. Homogenization gives degree-d forms Y_i; then
 E_i=(A_i+Y_i)/2, F_i=(A_i-Y_i)/2,
 E_i^2+F_i^2=R^2, sum E_i^2=R^2.
These identities hold globally as polynomial identities, including at excluded parameter values. If R,E_i,F_i all vanished at a complex projective parameter, A_i=E_i+F_i would also vanish, contradicting basepoint-freeness of the original map. Thus the lifted forms have no common basepoint. Original positivity, source, packet, content, orientation and canonical masks are still required for endpoints.


## 3. Odd parameter degree is impossible


At a real projective zero of R, sum E_i^2=0 forces every E_i=0; then E_i^2+F_i^2=0 forces every F_i=0. This is a forbidden common basepoint. Therefore R has no real projective zero. A nonzero real homogeneous form of odd degree satisfies R(-s,-t)=-R(s,t); continuity on the real unit circle forces a zero. R identically zero would force all lifted forms zero. Hence every basepoint-free map as above has even parameter degree.


This is a statement about global real/P1_Q parameter maps. It does not exclude all odd-degree algebraic curves, elliptic cubics, positive-genus curves, or isolated rational points on singular curves with nonrational normalization branches. Multiplying forms by a common polynomial does not change the minimal map degree and cannot circumvent the proof.


## 4. Degree two: every nonconstant lift has an identically zero edge


For d=2, R is a definite real quadratic. Change its overall sign if needed and write R=L*bar(L), where L and bar(L) are distinct complex linear forms. For each i,
 (E_i+iF_i)(E_i-iF_i)=L^2*bar(L)^2.
Neither factor is zero; unique factorization and conjugation leave exactly three allocations of the two quadratic factors: (L^2,bar(L)^2), (L*bar(L),L*bar(L)), or the reversed first allocation. In the middle case E_i=a_i R and F_i=b_i R, with a_i^2+b_i^2=1. In either other case, after absorbing the reversed allocation into conjugation,
 E_i=(c_i L^2+bar(c_i)bar(L)^2)/2, |c_i|=1.
Put z=L/bar(L), a nonconstant rational function. For m rotating coordinates, the identity sum E_i^2/R^2=1 becomes the Laurent identity
 m/2 + sum_fixed a_i^2 + (z^2 sum_rot c_i^2 + z^(-2) sum_rot bar(c_i)^2)/4 = 1.
Its coefficients imply sum_rot c_i^2=0 and m/2+sum_fixed a_i^2=1. The cases are exhaustive:
 - m=0: all coordinates proportional to R; the projective image is constant and the quadratic forms share R, so this is not a basepoint-free degree-two map.
 - m=1: c_i^2 cannot vanish, impossible.
 - m=3: the constant coefficient is3/2, impossible.
 - m=2: the sole fixed coordinate has a_k=0, so E_k is identically zero. The two rotating phases have opposite squares, giving the familiar boundary Pythagorean conic.
Therefore a nonconstant degree-two curve cannot have three strictly positive edges at any parameter. Boundary conics do exist: R=s^2+t^2, E=(t^2-s^2,2st,0), F=(2st,s^2-t^2,R). This example also satisfies the original signed plus identities with A=E+F,Y=E-F. It must not be discarded as an algebraic impossibility; positivity excludes it.


## 5. Exact receivers and limitations


A smooth geometrically irreducible Q-conic with a rational point has its degree-two rational parameterization by lines through that point. If such a conic is contained in P=0 and contains an eligible positive rational point, its open mask is generic, so sections2–4 give a contradiction. If it is not contained, pullback P is a nonzero homogeneous degree32 form and has at most32 distinct projective parameter roots. Uniqueness146 gives at most32 eligible endpoints on the conic, including the parameter at infinity. No height cutoff is needed for this occupancy bound.


A reducible conic of two Q-lines has at most32 eligible endpoints by145/146, and a doubled Q-line at most16. A conjugate pair of non-Q lines has at most one Q-point, their intersection: a rational point on one lies on its conjugate too. We do not exclude that isolated intersection as a physical point. These distinctions prevent applying the smooth parameter argument to a nonsplit singular conic.


More generally, a noncontained degree-d basepoint-free P1_Q parameter map has at most16d preimages, hence at most16d eligible endpoints. A contained generically open odd-degree map is impossible. For nonconstant contained P1_Q maps with potentially positive edges, the first remaining parameter degree is4. Quartic maps are NOT excluded. Curves of positive genus, nonsplit normalization issues and the number/cost of curves covering the Stage37 population remain unresolved. None of these occupancy constants establishes a global count or exponent saving.
